trends.name: Iran Nuclear Escalation & Oil Markets
trends.summary: Trump's April 6 pause on Iran energy attacks expires this weekend with Kharg Island as potential flashpoint. Real-time X posts show US oil surged above $95/barrel (+10% in 24hrs) as peace talks stall and Iran hardliners escalate nuclear rhetoric. Geopolitical risk is the dominant market driver with direct commodity and inflation implications.

trends.name: AI Infrastructure Crisis & Tech Investment Pivot
trends.summary: Major tech companies face a 'nuclear wall' on AI expansion due to lack of nuclear capacity, welders, and infrastructure—forcing strategic pivots. Meta pivots to West Texas ($10B AI data center boost), Apple opens Siri to rivals, and broader AI-to-reality gap is becoming an earnings/capex constraint. This signals potential margin pressure and capex disappointment ahead.

trends.name: Meta Stock Collapse & Regulatory Headwinds
trends.summary: Meta stock dropped 8% on two consecutive court defeats hitting Zuckerberg's recent momentum and credibility. Combines with broader tech selloff signals (Google breaking key support) and suggests regulatory/litigation risk is repricing mega-cap valuations downward. Key stock-specific risk event for tech-heavy portfolios.

trends.name: Recession Risk Resurfaces in Credit Markets
trends.summary: Goldman Sachs now pricing 30% US recession risk with slowing growth, 2.5% inflation, and 4.6% unemployment expectations. Credit spreads widening substantially despite no recession in base case—signals market uncertainty and potential credit stress ahead. Mortgage rates climbing for 4th straight week further pressures housing demand.

trends.name: SpaceX IPO Plans & Elon's X Restructuring
trends.summary: Elon Musk restructuring X ahead of SpaceX IPO with staff reductions (CMO and 20+ non-technical roles), focus on revenue growth, and delays in X Money compliance. Musk considering allocating 30% of SpaceX IPO to retail investors—major signal for 2026's blockbuster space IPO and Musk's strategic priorities.

trends.name: Mastercard Divests Real-Time Payments Division
trends.summary: Mastercard looking to divest real-time payments division acquired from NETS for $3.2B in 2019—signals strategy shift away from fintech consolidation and potential valuation reset. Market will scrutinize execution and pricing as payment landscape evolves.

trends.name: Pre-IPO AI Fund Collapse & Venture Repricing
trends.summary: Buzzy pre-IPO AI fund offering access to Anthropic and OpenAI is plummeting—signals venture/private market repricing and investor caution on unlisted AI plays. Suggests bubble risk in private AI valuations ahead of potential 2026 IPO wave.

trends.name: Crypto-Linked Equities Selloff & Stablecoin Legislation
trends.summary: Crypto-linked equities selling off as US stablecoin legislation stalls—regulatory uncertainty is depressing digital asset sentiment. Fannie Mae's acceptance of first crypto-backed mortgage product shows some progress but overall headwinds dominate.

trends.name: Defense & Ukraine War Economics
trends.summary: G7 foreign ministers collaborating on Chornobyl nuclear plant repairs (estimated €500M) with EBRD funding—signals sustained defense/Ukraine aid commitments and infrastructure investment themes. Geopolitical capital spending will remain elevated.

trends.name: Labor Market Tightness & Wage Pressure Persists
trends.summary: US labor market showing 'countercurrents'—United Airlines flight attendants reached first pandemic-era raises, BoC warns of structural inflation risks from energy prices and tight labor. Despite softening signals, wage momentum remains sticky, complicating Fed rate-cut narrative.

trends.name: Netflix Price Hikes & Streaming Economics Shift
trends.summary: Netflix raising prices across all streaming plans—signals confidence in demand elasticity and margin expansion despite macro concerns. Reflects broader streaming industry shift toward profitability over subscriber growth, with potential consumer pushback risk.

trends.name: Medical School Antitrust Investigation & Education Policy
trends.summary: DOJ opened antitrust investigations into Stanford, Ohio State, and UC San Diego medical school admissions policies with April 24 data deadline—signals potential broad education sector scrutiny and policy risk. Threatens federal funding if compliance fails.
